title: Childhood memories: climbing on the casket and the red-hot stove
summary: At five or six he fell climbing on his mother's casket and put his face on a red-hot pot-belly stove without a scar.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: But getting back to this early childhood, I remember that and then about my mother being in the hospital, then later on during that same period I remember trying to climb up on the casket in the home where the body was for viewing, and you know. And I remember just as well as if it was yesterday, I climbed up on the casket and fell in the process, which naturally caused a lot of commotion in the house during the days of this -- before the ceremonial procedures for the funeral. And during that same period crawling on the floor I put my face on a red hot stove. Now, this I don't understand how this happened and how there's not a scar, there's not a mark on my face. I don't know how this happened. But I crawled into this red hot stove. I remember seeing these stoves in the old days where you used coal around --
